diagnosis_summary: Rock maintainers confirmed that the Rock 19.2 WebForms Workflow Entry path hydrated the workflow before sending the final form notification, which cleared the Action and Activity objects needed by Action.FormAttributes. Commit 2065cc9 preserves those completed objects across hydration and restores them before rendering the notification and confirmation. Maintainers did not reproduce the defect in the Obsidian workflow entry path, and no stock communication-template change is required. The issue is labeled Fixed in v19.4; verify exact package inclusion because a release-line label is not an exact build attestation.
workaround_summaries: Use a Rock build proven to contain commit 2065cc91efd198f4d5f22f4d523a569c5600a6a7. If an interim template workaround is unavoidable, clone the stock communication and use an explicit allowlist of approved workflow attribute keys; never render the full Workflow.AttributeValues collection without review because it is broader than the submitted form.

verification_playbook.goal: Determine whether the instance uses the affected WebForms notification path and lacks the completed-object hydration fix, without submitting a form or sending an email.
prerequisites: Know the exact installed Rock version.
Have read-only access to the selected Form Builder notification communication.

steps.title: Check build ancestry and entry path
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the installed package contains commit 2065cc91efd198f4d5f22f4d523a569c5600a6a7 and whether the form uses the affected WebForms Workflow Entry path rather than the Obsidian path.
steps.expected_if_affected: The instance uses the WebForms path on Rock 19.2 or another build that lacks the completed-object hydration fix.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: The installed build contains the fixing commit or an independently verified equivalent, or the workflow uses the Obsidian path where maintainers did not reproduce the defect.

steps.title: Inspect the selected template contract
steps.instructions: Return only the two Boolean indicators. Do not return the communication body or any submitted workflow values.
steps.probe: SELECT TOP (1) CASE WHEN [Body] LIKE '%Action.FormAttributes%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS UsesActionFormAttributes, CASE WHEN [Body] LIKE '%Workflow.AttributeValues%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS UsesWorkflowAttributeValues FROM [SystemCommunication] WHERE [Guid] = 'D5414D4F-538E-4578-8330-D6CA8FD5F664'
steps.expected_if_affected: UsesActionFormAttributes is 1 while the affected WebForms source is installed, establishing the template and source preconditions without rendering submitted values.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: The stock communication is absent or customized. That changes applicability and requires reviewing the selected template; it does not establish that the source defect is absent.

steps.title: Inspect the form notification selection
steps.instructions: Open the form's Communications configuration without saving and confirm whether Notification Email uses the stock Form Submission Result communication or a customized replacement.
steps.expected_if_affected: Notification Email selects the stock template or a copy that still reads Action.FormAttributes.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: Notification Email is disabled or uses a separately verified template and merge-field strategy.

limitations: A definitive render test requires a form submission and email delivery, so it must use isolated staging and non-real recipients rather than this production-safe playbook.
Template inspection cannot prove whether a specific workflow action resolves FormAttributes at runtime.
Maintainers reproduced this in WebForms only; do not generalize the affected assertion to Obsidian Workflow Entry.

context.scope: WebForms Workflow Entry Form Builder notification using Action.FormAttributes
exact WebForms Workflow Entry source revision; release-package inclusion remains independently verifiable
official fix release line for the WebForms Workflow Entry path; verify the exact installed package
